div.ab: ⁊ beo ðam halgum tidan, ealswa hit riht is, eallum Cristenum mannum sib ⁊ som gemæne, ⁊ ælc sacu getwæmed.
⁊ beo þam halgan tidan, ealswa hit riht is, eallum Cristenum mannum sib ⁊ sóm gemæne, ⁊ ælc sacu getwæmed.
⁊ beo ðam halgum tidan, ealswa hit riht is, eallum Cristenum mannum sóm ⁊ sib gemæne, ⁊ ælc sacu getwæmed.
⁊ beo ðam halgum tidan, ealswa hit riht is, eallum Cristenum mannum sóm ⁊ sib gemæne, ⁊ ælc sacu getwæmed.
And beo ðam halgum tidan, ealswa hit riht is, eallum Cristenum mannum sib and som gemæne, and ælc sacu getwæmed.
Und an den heiligen Festen sei, wie es recht ist, allen christlichen Menschen Friede und Eintracht gemeinsam und jeder Rechtsstreit eingestellt.
And at the holy seasons, as is right, let there be peace and concord among all Christian people, and every lawsuit suspended.
And at the holy festivals, as is fitting, there shall be peace and concord among all Christian men, and every dispute shall be laid aside.
And at these holy seasons, as it is right, there is to be peace and unity among all Christian men, and every suit is to be laid aside.
And at holy times, just as is proper, there is to be peace and friendship among all Christians, and each dispute is to be resolved.

note.seg: Nicht schon eine königsgesetzliche Treuga, wie Huberti Gottesfrieden I 249 meint. Denn ein Fehderecht war in England nicht anerkannt; zweitens stimmt das Fehlen der Strafbestimmung mehr zu geistlicher Ermahnung; drittens lässt das Folgen des Prozesses vermuten, es sei, wie in 13, 1. 18, nur gerichtlicher Streit samt berechtigter Rache in Selbsthilfe verboten.—S. Gl Treuga Dei 1. a

Not yet a Treuga established by royal law, as Huberti Gottesfrieden I 249 thinks. For a right of feud was not recognised in England; secondly, the absence of a penal provision accords better with ecclesiastical exhortation; thirdly, the reference to legal proceedings that follows suggests that, as in 13, 1. 18, only litigation, together with justified revenge by self-help, is forbidden.—See Gl Treuga Dei 1. a

Die Rechtspflicht geht laut 20 weiter, ihre Erfüllung ist nur verschoben, unterbrochen. Aus Wbb. allerdings ist nur die nächstverwandte Bed. ‘geschlichtet, beigelegt’ belegt

tollatur I Cn 17, 2 Q, segregatur Cons, ‘lifted’ Schmid, ‘removed’ Toller 1008, less well ‘appeased’ Price-Thorpe, Toller 461. According to 20 the legal obligation continues; its fulfilment is only postponed, interrupted. From the dictionaries, admittedly, only the closely related meaning ‘settled, composed’ is attested
Cf. VI, 25, 1; I Cn. 17, 2; Can. Edg. 23; Eccles. Insts. 42, ed. Thorpe, ii. pp. 248, 438; Wulfstan, p. 118.
